sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Arrays are your first step into organizing data like a pro! Let's explore how they work and why they're essential.

• What arrays are and why we need them
• How to create and use arrays in code
• Simple real-world examples to make it click

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a toolbox with labeled slots - that's an array! Each slot holds one item, and you can access any item instantly by its number.

Arrays are like:
• A row of mailboxes (each with a number)
• A parking lot (each spot has a number)
• A classroom (each seat is numbered)

In programming, arrays let you store multiple values of the same type together. Instead of creating 10 separate variables for 10 numbers, you create one array that holds all 10 numbers!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: An array stores a fixed-size collection of elements of the same type
Arrays solve the problem of managing many related values without separate variables
Array elements are accessed by a zero-based index: first element is at index 0
The length of an array is fixed once created and is accessed via array.length
Arrays are reference types, so a variable holds a reference to the array object

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Arrays store multiple values in one variable. Always remember: first element is at index 0. Practice creating and accessing arrays. Ready to learn about loops with arrays next.
